Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 5 along with accused No.1 have been charge sheeted for the offence under Sections 498 A, 323, 504 and 506 read with section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act alleging that the defacto complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1, and the accused No.2 and 3 are the parent-in laws, accused No.4 is sister-in-law and accused No.5 is the uncle of accused No.1, and she was subjected to cruelty both mentally and physically and demand was made to bring money from the parental home.

sentences.text:
Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition by accused Nos.2 to 5.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. A perusal of the FIR lodged by respondent No.2 indicates that there are no specific allegations as against accused Nos.2 to 5, as to how, and in what manner, they subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also does not disclose there was a demand made to bring money from the parental home.

The FIR indicates that accused Nos.2 to 5 are permanent residents of Dharwad, and the defacto complainant has led the marital life in Bangalore along with accused No.1 which clearly implies that accused Nos.2 to 5 were not staying along with accused No.1 and defacto complainant in the matrimonial home.

4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar1 at para No.18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

5. In view of the preceding analysis, I am of the view that the police have laid charge sheet only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations, and in the absence of any corroborative material, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioners/accused will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly,
I pass the following :
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.20644/2015 on the file of III ACMM,
Bengaluru insofar as accused Nos.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.
